title: Procurement pricing variance & billing acceleration procedures (2026)
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
This playbook documents the approved procedure for handling pricing variances discovered during procurement and the conditions and operational steps to accelerate billing (shorten payment terms or issue interim invoices) for contracted Dedicated and Hosted customers. It clarifies roles, thresholds, required artifacts, operational SLAs, and accounting (revrec) treatment.

Purpose
- Reduce time-to-billing when price or volume changes require invoice timing adjustments.
- Provide a consistent approval and audit trail so revenue recognition remains compliant with ASC 606 and internal control standards.
- Minimize customer disruption while protecting company margin and cash flow.

Scope
Applies to: dedicated-capacity and hosted subscriptions, multi-month purchase orders, professional services add-ons, and third-party hardware/software pass-throughs where a pricing variance or accelerated billing is requested. Excludes pure one-time refunds and simple credit memos processed under the existing billing adjustments SOP.

Definitions
- Pricing variance: any negotiated deviation from the originally executed contract pricing (discount increases, fee add-ons, or material scope changes > 5% of contract value).
- Billing acceleration: moving invoice issuance earlier than originally scheduled, shortening payment terms (e.g., Net30 -> Net15), or issuing interim milestone invoices.
- Material change threshold: dollar-amount or percentage that requires tiered approvals (see matrix).

Owners and RACI
- Requestor (R): Sales / Customer Success / Solutions Engineering initiates the request and uploads the change packet.
- Legal (A/R): Reviews contract language and approves amendments. (Accountable for contract form).
- Finance Ops (A/C): Reviews accounting impact, approves billing timing and revrec treatment, issues invoices. (Consulted on margin and cash flow).
- Procurement (C): For pass-throughs or vendor pricing changes, verifies PO alignment.
- CRO/Sales Leader (I/A): Approves commercial concessions above delegated limits.
- Audit & Compliance (I): Receives final artifact for internal control records.

Approval Matrix (text table)
- Tier 0: Non-material variance (< $5k or < 5% of MRR) -> Sales Ops approval. Finance Ops notified within 3 business days.
- Tier 1: Minor variance ($5k–$50k or 5%–20% of MRR) -> Sales Leader + Finance Ops approval. Legal informed.
- Tier 2: Major variance ($50k–$250k or 20%–50% of MRR) -> CRO + Finance Ops + Legal signoff; Procurement review if pass-through.
- Tier 3: Strategic (> $250k or > 50% of MRR) -> Executive review (CFO + Chief Legal Officer + CRO). Requires written memo and finance modeling.

Pricing Variance - Required Artifacts
1) Change packet (uploaded to Contracting JIRA ticket): redline amendment, summary memo from Account Executive, customer approval email.
2) Updated pricing schedule (CSV) showing prior vs. proposed pricing by SKU and usage band.
3) RevRec impact memo (Finance Ops template) with estimated revenue and timing delta.
4) Procurement confirmation for any third-party cost changes (vendor notice, updated PO).

Billing Acceleration Triggers
- Trigger A (Operational): customer requests earlier billing to match internal capital planning. Allowed for Tier 0–1 with Sales Ops + Finance Ops signoff.
- Trigger B (Contractual): contract amendment explicitly permits milestone or accelerated billing. Billing proceeds per amendment.
- Trigger C (Risk Mitigation): vendor price increases that would retroactively reduce margin and where contract allows pass-through; accelerated billing considered to lock in pre-increase rates (requires Procurement + Finance Ops approval).
- Trigger D (Cash/Collection risk): customer downgrade or late-payment history; billing acceleration may be used as a credit control measure subject to CRO and Finance Ops approval.

Operational Procedure (step-by-step)
1) Initiation: Requestor opens a Contracting JIRA (project: CONTRACT-CHANGE) with label "pricing-variance" and attaches the change packet.
2) Triage (SLA: 2 business days): Sales Ops assigns Tier and routes to Finance Ops & Legal. Automated notifications are sent to reviewers.
3) Analysis (SLA: 5 business days for Tier 0–1, 10 business days for Tier 2–3): Finance Ops completes revrec memo and margin impact. Legal drafts amendment redline.
4) Approval: Approvers sign in the Contracting system. Electronic signatures permitted for Tier 0–1; Tier 2–3 require recorded meeting approval and an executive memo.
5) Billing Setup (SLA: 2 business days after approval): Finance Ops creates new invoice schedule in the billing system (Billing Service v2) and sets payment terms. If acceleration is approved, update AR aging buckets and notify Treasury for cash forecasting.
6) Notification: Customer is sent a formal notice with updated invoice and payment terms; customer confirmation required for Net-change in payment terms.
7) Recording & Archive: Save final amendment, invoices, and revrec memo to the Contracts bucket (S3 path: s3://redwood-contracts/archived/2026/) and add link to the JIRA ticket. Compliance closes loop.

Accounting and RevRec Guidance
- Shortening payment terms alone does not change revenue recognition timing; revrec follows performance obligations. However, if acceleration triggers earlier invoicing for a deliverable already satisfied by Redwood, Revenue may be recognized earlier — Finance Ops must consult ASC 606 checklist and document justification in the revrec memo.
- Deposit accounting: accelerated prepayments that create a contract liability must be tracked in the Billing Service as "deferred_revenue_accelerated" and reconciled monthly.
- Hedge scenarios: when vendor cost increases are passed through, record an offsetting COGS entry immediately on invoice issuance and document margin pass-through in the revrec memo.

System Controls and Audit Trail
- Mandatory fields in Contracting JIRA: requestor, estimated variance amount, requested acceleration date, link to amendment draft, assigned approvers.
- Billing Service audit log must contain: billing change id, approver id, timestamp, previous payment terms.
- Monthly sampling: Audit & Compliance will sample 10% of accelerated billing cases for the quarter and report exceptions.

Sample billing API snippet (Billing Service v2)
```
POST /v2/invoices
{
  "customer_id": "cust_1234",
  "contract_id": "ctr_5678",
  "invoice_schedule": "accelerated",
  "payment_terms": "Net15",
  "line_items": [ { "sku": "dedicated-gpu-hr", "qty": 1, "unit_price": 50000 } ],
  "approval_reference": "CONTRACT-CHANGE-9876"
}
```

Exceptions and Escalations
- If Legal determines the amendment introduces unacceptable legal risk, the request is rejected and a remediation plan must be produced within 7 business days.
- If Finance Ops is asked to accelerate billing but cannot reconcile the revrec impact, Finance Ops must escalate to the CFO within 48 hours.

Templates and Checklists (links)
- RevRec impact template: /templates/finance/revrec-impact-template.xlsx
- Amendment redline template: /templates/legal/amendment-redline.docx
- Billing acceleration request checklist: /templates/procurement/billing-acceleration-checklist.md

Metrics and SLAs
- Triage SLA: 2 business days.
- Approval SLA: 5 business days (Tier 0–1), 10 business days (Tier 2–3).
- Billing execution SLA: 2 business days after approval.
- Success metrics: percentage of accelerated bills issued within SLA (> 95%), number of revrec restatements related to acceleration (target 0).

Related Procedures
- See: commitment-lifecycle-credit-and-sunsetting-policy (revrec lifecycle) and purchase-requisition-risk-tiering-sla-and-escalation (procurement risk) for upstream inputs.

Revision history
- 2026-01-15: Initial draft by Maya Chen.
- 2026-03-02: Added Tier 3 executive review requirement (reviewers: Santiago Ruiz, Priya Kapoor).
- 2026-05-03: Updated SLAs and added Billing Service API snippet; set confidentiality to restricted.

Appendix: Quick decision flow (text)
1) Is the variance material? -> Yes -> follow Tier matrix; No -> Sales Ops handles.
2) Does the customer require earlier invoicing? -> Yes -> follow Billing Acceleration Triggers.
3) Is there vendor pass-through? -> Yes -> Procurement verifies and Finance adjusts COGS.
